newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia's central bank intervenes in forex market.
newsitem.headline: Croatia's central bank intervenes in forex market.

text.p: Croatia's central bank said on Tuesday it had intervened in the foreign exchange market by buying and selling German marks.
"We had two goals: to prevent (the kuna) exchange rate appreciation due to stronger currency inflow and to help liquidity of the money market," a bank official told Reuters.
The bank bought 11.1 million marks at an average rate of 3.5700 kuna, it said in a statement faxed to Reuters.
This will result in an injection of just under 40 million kuna into the hard-pressed banking sector in two days. But there was no immediate reaction from the money market.

The official said this type of intervention would be more frequent during the summer as more hard currency from tourism createS an increased demand for kuna by banks and exchange offices, boosting upward pressure on the kuna rate.
The bank today also sold two million marks at the same average rate of 3.5700 kuna per mark, it said.
